findings.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization flow for each customer workspace
findings.detail: OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol. Public integrations can be installed in any workspace within their installation scope. The flow returns an access token used for API requests on behalf of the authorizing user.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations or workspaces connect to the app.

findings.title: Use a public integration for connections from any workspace
findings.detail: A scoped integration can be installed only in selected workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make the app available to any workspace, create a public integration. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers in other organizations or workspaces will connect.

findings.title: Read content capability for page titles and content
findings.detail: Calling the page retrieval and page markdown endpoints requires the connection to have read content capabilities. Without that capability the API returns 403. This capability is limited to pages the user has shared with the connection.
findings.appliesWhen: The app reads titles and content of shared pages and does not create or modify pages.

evidence.quote: your connection, open the Configuration tab, and scroll to the Capabilities section. Attempting to call this endpoint without read content capabilities returns an HTTP response with a 403 status code.
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Pages must be selected in the page picker and shared with the connection
findings.detail: During authorization the user selects pages in the page picker. The picker only shows pages to which the user has full access. If a page is not shared with the connection, API requests for it return an error.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer chooses which pages the app can read.

evidence.quote: Once the connection is shared, you can start making API requests. If the page is not shared, any API requests made will respond with an error.

findings.appliesWhen: Multiple members of a customer workspace will use the app.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
steps.detail: In the Developer portal, go to Build > Connections and create a public integration so customers in any workspace can install it. Enter the connection name, development workspace and redirect URI, then enable the read content capability. Installation scope cannot be changed after creation.
steps.doneWhen: A public OAuth connection exists with a redirect URI and the read content capability enabled, and its OAuth client ID and secret are available on the Configuration tab.

steps.title: Send a test user through the consent flow and verify the callback
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser as a test user. Choose the pages to share in the page picker, approve, and confirm Notion redirects to the registered redirect URI with a code query parameter. Denial returns an error parameter instead.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URI receives a code parameter after approval, and the state value matches the value sent. A cancelled test returns error=access_denied.

steps.title: Read a shared page as markdown and re-request unknown blocks
steps.detail: Call the page markdown endpoint with markdown_version=v2 for a page the test user shared. If the response has truncated=true, re-request each returned unknown_block_ids value through the same endpoint, treating object_not_found for those IDs as expected inaccessible content. Do not request any write operation.
steps.doneWhen: The response has object page_markdown and a non-empty markdown field for the shared test page; for each truncated response, every unknown_block_ids value was re-requested and object_not_found results were handled gracefully. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /v1/pages/{id}/markdown and no page creation, modification or workspace administration calls.

steps.title: Read a shared page's title property
steps.detail: Retrieve the page object for the shared test page with filter_properties=title. The title is in properties.title.title, a rich text array; join all text segments by plain_text. Pages outside a data source show only the title property.
steps.doneWhen: The response object is page and properties.title.title contains the expected title text joined from all array elements. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing request log contains only the GET request to /v1/pages/{id} and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: For a page in a data source, the property values follow that data source’s schema . For a page whose parent is another page, the only property is title .
